Boundary Artifact Matrix

For each 800-53A subpart: the evidence that satisfies it, whether it comes from policy or the boundary, who owns it, and which provider (CSP, an enterprise service, the organization, or the boundary) likely delivers it. Edit any row to match your inheritance model; changes are saved here for everyone with access, and every view exports to CSV, Excel, or JSON.

Comes from

  • Org policy: set once by the organization and inherited. The boundary cites it.
  • Boundary: only the system team can produce it.
  • Shared: org supplies the standard, template, or service; the boundary produces the system instance or evidence.
  • Common control: provided and assessed by a common control provider (facilities, enterprise PKI, ICAM).

ODP rows

Organization-defined parameters are the cleanest line between policy and boundary. Values that apply everywhere (review frequencies, notification roles, training cadence) belong in policy or a standard. Values that depend on the system (component attributes, ports, event lists) get a floor from policy and a system value in the SSP parameter table. Under FedRAMP, the FedRAMP baseline fixes many of these values for you.

Likely provider

  • CSP (inherited): physical, hardware, and hosting-layer controls. Cite the CSP's FedRAMP package and customer responsibility matrix.
  • CSP + boundary: the CSP offers the capability; the boundary must enable and evidence it.
  • Enterprise: …: an agency service you leverage (identity, SOC, PKI, LMS, HR). "Boundary +" means you still owe the system-specific part.
  • Organization: policy, program, and AO decisions.

Keeping it current

Edit a row with its Edit button, or export to Excel, change the Comes from, Responsible party, Likely provider, Evidence artifact, or Notes columns, and import the file back. Only rows that differ from the current matrix are saved, and Reset returns a row to its default. Export "Changes only" to keep your tailoring in version control.

How this was built

Every statement ID, statement, ODP, baseline tag, and examine-object list comes from NIST's published OSCAL SP 800-53 Rev 5 catalog and baseline profiles. The evidence kind, source, and party are a first-pass assignment from rules over the statement text and family. Treat them as a draft to tailor to your organization's inheritance model, not as NIST guidance.
